title: Bernadette
hookLine: Catholics tell of a poor, sickly girl at Lourdes to whom Mary appeared, and of a spring the sick still come to

lines: A LADY IN WHITE IN THE GROTTO.
cards: Cold water, a riverbank, a girl gathering firewood and bones to sell. That's how the story begins, as Catholics tell it. Her name is Bernadette Soubirous.
Her family is poor enough to be living in a former jail cell in Lourdes, in the south of France. She is small, often sick, and can barely read.
Near a rocky hollow by the river, a grotto, she says she sees a lady dressed in white, with a rosary. Nobody else sees anything. Her mother is worried, the town curious, the police suspicious.

teach.b: The spring comes first. In Bernadette's account, the lady told her to drink from the spring and wash in it. There was no spring she could see.
So she dug in the muddy ground with her hands, and the crowd thought she had lost her mind. Then water began to flow, and it still flows. Then the name.
For a long time the lady didn't say who she was.
When Bernadette finally asked, she reported the answer in her local dialect: I am the Immaculate Conception.
She said she didn't know what the words meant, and repeated them all the way to the priest so she wouldn't forget.
In Catholic teaching, the Immaculate Conception means Mary was kept free from original sin from the moment her life began. Here the churches differ.
The Catholic Church investigated, and judged that the appearances could be believed. It also teaches that no Catholic is required to believe in private revelations like this one.
Orthodox Christians honor Mary deeply, but describe her holiness in their own terms. Protestant churches don't treat visions like this as part of their teaching. And Bernadette?
She didn't stay to be well-known. She became a nun, far from Lourdes, often ill, and the Catholic Church later named her a saint.
At the spring, the sick are brought to pray and to bathe, and the Church examines claims of healing carefully.

Christians in other churches pray for the sick too, as the letter of James describes, in the King James Bible: "Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him."

how: Catholic pilgrims travel to Lourdes to pray at the grotto, join candlelight processions and bathe in the spring water, and the sick are brought there with volunteers who help care for them.

games.q: you're Bernadette. the police and the priest question you again and again, and many want you to take it back. what do you do?
o: say you made it all up, so they'll leave you alone.
tell the same story again, simply.
refuse to say anything at all.
games.why: in the Catholic telling, she kept to her story, plainly, without dressing it up, and kept going back to the grotto.

practice: Bring to mind one person who is sick right now, and picture them, not their illness, them. Then add someone sick whom nobody is praying for, a stranger in a ward somewhere.
If you pray, hold them both before God, or, if it's your way, ask Mary to pray for them; if you don't, simply wish them strength.

wordCard.voice: Bernadette. A poor, sickly girl from Lourdes who said Mary appeared to her at a grotto, and who dug in the mud until water came.

carryVoice: Your line: the spring at the grotto. It began with a girl digging in mud. See you tomorrow.
